The estate lies just outside the DOC subregions and is labelled Alentejano.

sites.name: Herdade do Esporão
sites.text: A huge estate with a medieval tower, bought in the 1970s by José Roquette's family, planted from the 1980s and now among Portugal's biggest wine groups (also owning Quinta dos Murças in the Douro and Quinta do Ameal in Vinho Verde). Australian winemaker David Baverstock shaped its style from 1992. Esporão is a leader in organic farming and keeps a large ampelographic collection of Portuguese and foreign varieties.

sites.name: Adega da Cartuxa
sites.class: Fundação Eugénio de Almeida winery, Évora
sites.text: The Fundação Eugénio de Almeida's cellars, in a former Jesuit retreat house just outside Évora, beside the Carthusian monastery of Scala Coeli. Here are made Cartuxa and Pêra-Manca, released only in great years and among Portugal's most sought-after reds.

sites.name: Villa Romana de São Cucufate
sites.text: The ruins of a large Roman villa, rebuilt in the 4th century, with storerooms and evidence of wine and olive oil production; later a monastery. It anchors the talha wine tradition of nearby Vila de Frades.

sites.name: Vila de Frades (talha wine village)
sites.text: A village near Vidigueira whose adegas and taverns still ferment wine in clay talhas; every November, around St Martin's Day, the talhas are opened and the new wine is served from the jar. Producers such as Honrado, Gerações da Talha and Herdade do Rocim have helped it become a recognised style.

sites.name: Herdade do Rocim
sites.text: A modern estate between Vidigueira and Cuba that hosts the Amphora Wine Day each November and makes several talha wines alongside fresh Antão Vaz whites.

sites.name: Herdade do Peso
sites.text: Sogrape's estate near Vidigueira, on the plains below the fault scarp, making Vinha do Monte and Herdade do Peso wines.

sites.name: Adega Cooperativa de Vidigueira, Cuba e Alvito
sites.text: The Vidigueira cooperative, one of the main producers of Antão Vaz whites below the fault scarp, and a keeper of the local talha wine tradition.

sites.name: Adega de Borba
sites.text: Founded in 1955, the Borba cooperative was one of the first in the Alentejo to bottle quality wine; its red Reserva with the cork-oak label became a national classic.

sites.name: Quinta do Mouro
sites.text: Miguel Louro's estate on schist near Estremoz, which in the 1990s showed that the Alentejo could make structured, age-worthy reds; known for its Alicante Bouschet and the 'Erro' wines. Point approximate (near Estremoz).

sites.name: Tapada do Chaves
sites.text: A historic estate near Portalegre whose old vineyards on the granite foothills of the Serra de São Mamede made some of the Alentejo's most long-lived reds in the late 20th century; now owned by Fundação Eugénio de Almeida (Cartuxa).

sites.name: Quinta da Fonte Souto
sites.text: The Symingtons' first property outside the Douro, bought in 2017 on the slopes of the Serra de São Mamede near Marvão, at about 500 to 600 m; cool, granite and schist vineyards for fresh Alentejo whites and reds. Point at the Fonte Souto locality.

sites.name: Tapada de Coelheiros
sites.text: An estate near Igrejinha (Arraiolos), founded in the 1980s, among the first Alentejo producers of single-estate Cabernet blends and Chardonnay; now in Brazilian ownership.

sites.name: Herdade dos Grous
sites.text: A large estate and agritourism hotel south of Beja, outside the DOC subregions, known for Moon Harvested wines and ripe reds.

sites.name: Adega Mayor
sites.text: The winery of the Delta coffee group in Campo Maior, designed by the architect Álvaro Siza Vieira and opened in 2007; a white concrete block on the plain near the Spanish border.

sites.name: Monsaraz
sites.text: A fortified medieval village on a hill above the Reguengos vineyards and the Alqueva reservoir, western Europe's largest artificial lake, whose irrigation water has changed Alentejo farming.

sites.name: Adega de Lagoa
sites.text: The historic Lagoa cooperative, founded in 1945 and once the main producer of Algarve wine, including an aged dry fortified wine.

sites.name: Morgado do Quintão
sites.text: A family estate near Estômbar with Negra Mole vines over a century old; its pale, savoury reds have revived interest in the Algarve's native grape.

sites.name: Adega do Cantor
sites.text: The winery at Guia, Albufeira, founded in partnership with the singer Sir Cliff Richard, whose Vida Nova wines helped draw attention to the Algarve in the 2000s.

sites.name: Quinta do Francês
sites.text: A small estate in the hills above Silves making Syrah, Touriga Nacional and Aragonez blends.

sites.name: Landscape of the Pico Island Vineyard Culture
sites.text: A 987-ha listed landscape on Pico's west coast: thousands of currais, rectangular pens of black basalt built from the 15th century to shield vines from wind and spray, plus manor houses, wine cellars, wells, ramps and tiny harbours. The Lajido da Criação Velha trail crosses its heart.

sites.name: Lajido de Santa Luzia
sites.text: A hamlet on Pico's north coast built of black lava, among walled vineyards and the old cellars and stills of the Verdelho trade; part of the UNESCO landscape.

sites.name: Museu do Vinho do Pico
sites.text: In an old Carmelite convent estate in Madalena, with a dragon-tree grove, a traditional still and displays on the island's Verdelho history.

sites.name: Azores Wine Company
sites.text: Founded in 2014 by António Maçanita, Filipe Rocha and Paulo Machado, the company has replanted abandoned currais and makes dry Arinto dos Açores, Terrantez do Pico and Verdelho that have put Azores wine on top wine lists. Its winery in Bandeiras, opened in the early 2020s, is clad in black basalt.

sites.name: Cooperativa Vitivinícola da Ilha do Pico
sites.text: The island cooperative in Madalena, which kept Pico wine alive through the late 20th century and produces the Frei Gigante and Terras de Lava ranges.

sites.name: Museu do Vinho dos Biscoitos
sites.text: The Brum family's wine house and museum in Biscoitos, which has made fortified Verdelho on Terceira since 1890 and documents the island's lava-field vineyards.

sites.name: Adega Cooperativa da Graciosa
sites.text: The cooperative of Santa Cruz da Graciosa that makes most of the island's DOC white wine.
